answer: A sybil farmer's edge is holding ten thousand identity slots for nearly nothing. Price every slot like a walnut orchard under Harberger rules: each identity self-assesses its slot's value, pays a continuous tax on that price, and anyone may buy the slot at the stated price. Price low and the farm gets bought out from under it; price at the true zenith of its earning power and ten thousand slots bleed tax faster than any echo of cloned work can refill them. One honest agent pays one small honest tax -- a farm pays the market's verdict on every ghost it holds.
